claims.text: In-situ high-resolution TEM combined with EDS or APT can reveal oxidation-induced elemental redistribution in the alloy's dual nanoprecipitates.
During high-temperature oxidation, the dual nanoprecipitates undergo dynamic elemental redistribution.
Cr and Ti are among the elements redistributed during oxidation.
Cr and Ti are oxidation-resistant elements in this context.
Elemental redistribution from the nanoprecipitates leads to formation of a protective oxide scale.
The additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy exhibits dual nanoprecipitation.
The additively manufactured alloy has enhanced strength relative to cast and wrought counterparts.
Controlled thermal cycling can simulate high-temperature service environments relevant to gas turbines, power plants, and aerospace components.
Nanoprecipitates act as sites for elemental segregation.
Nanoprecipitate-matrix boundaries act as sites for interfacial oxide formation.
Oxidation drives key elements such as Cr and Ti from nanoprecipitates toward an oxide layer.
Redistributed elements form a continuous or protective oxide layer that influences overall oxidation behavior.
Oxidation will produce time-resolved changes in nanoprecipitate size, morphology, and elemental composition.
Cr and/or Ti will segregate at precipitate-oxide interfaces.
Interfacial Cr and/or Ti segregation will correlate with improved formation of a protective oxide scale.
Dynamic elemental redistribution is less pronounced in cast and wrought versions of the alloy.
Oxide-scale formation is less effective in cast and wrought versions of the alloy.
